text:
The strongest ground is that the debtor's August 1 oral promise to pay a debt already barred by the statute of limitations is unenforceable because the applicable statute (often a revival statute or statute of frauds provision) requires a signed writing for such a promise. Although a new promise can revive a time-barred debt under the moral-obligation doctrine, many jurisdictions impose formal writing requirements, and an oral promise fails those requirements.  
CONFIDENCE: 78
